subject: Post-call: POC success criteria & proposed model/fallback grid
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Reed <alison.reed@lighthouse-retail.com>, Markus Engel <markus.engel@lighthouse-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: POC success criteria & proposed model/fallback grid

Hi Alison / Markus —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we can get the POC moving next week. I captured what I heard and a concrete success statement for the trial: please review and flag anything missing.

POC objective
- Validate a lightweight intent-extraction + chat assistant for in-store checkout support (voice transcripts -> suggested responses / SKU lookups).

Proposed success criteria (metric-driven)
- Intent classification accuracy (macro F1) >= 0.92 on your internal sample set (English + Spanish).
- Average end-to-end latency <= 350 ms p95 for single-turn requests when served from Redwood Dedicated in us-west region.
- Resolver accuracy for SKU lookup >= 98% for top-100 SKUs.
- Human-in-the-loop escalation rate <= 6% for low-confidence responses.
- No PII persisted in hosted logs; audit trail available for sampled requests.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): exchange prompt set & sample transcripts (you to send).
- Week 1: Redwood spins up trial endpoints, baseline model runs on 1k transcripts.
- Week 2: Joint evaluation of metrics & latency; iterate prompts and routing.
- Week 3: Final acceptance run and handoff for pilot planning.

Model selection (initial + fallback)
- Primary candidate: MPT-7B-Instruct (fp16) — chosen for a balance of instruction-following and cost for short-form dialogue.
- Fallback: Llama-13B-Quant (8-bit quantized) — used only if capacity constraints or to meet latency SLO during peak.
- Multilingual approach: run primary model for EN/ES; for FR/DE we will route to a small translation-first pipeline (low volume) — we can expand if required.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood: Ben Carter (technical lead) and Marissa Cole (evaluation lead).
- Lighthouse: Alison (POC owner) and Markus (platform integration).

Next steps (asks)
1) Alison — please drop the sample transcript + SKU list (top 100) as discussed; the prompt set template is attached.
2) Agree on a test account for Dedicated capacity (we can provision a short trial).
3) Confirm SSO and IP allowlist details for secure endpoints.

I've attached a simple prompt set template and a draft timeline. If that all looks good, Ben and I will schedule a short kickoff for Monday (30 min) to allocate owners and spin up the trial infra.

Thanks —
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai/
From: Alison Reed <alison.reed@lighthouse-retail.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Engel <markus.engel@lighthouse-retail.com>
Date: 2029-03-18T13:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC success criteria & proposed model/fallback grid

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers inline and a few clarifications: 

> POC objective
Sounds right. We'll scope to checkout-support only (not returns) for the POC.

> Success criteria
- Intent accuracy target: 0.92 is fine. We'll run a pre-POC labeling pass and share ground truth.
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms — can you confirm whether that includes network to our office in Portland (we can do a baseline from a customer device)?
- SKU resolver accuracy: yes, 98% target ok.

Attachments: uploaded the transcript sample and SKU top100 in the attached workbook. Also included a short list of edge cases we want stressed.

Questions:
1) For fallback model: what are the expected cost delta and any differences in hallucination profile between MPT-7B-Instruct and the Llama-13B-Quant?
2) For Spanish: our storefront uses regional slang in certain markets. Is there an easy way to add a small lexicon and test without full re-tuning?

We can confirm the test Dedicated account — Markus will share network allowlist and SSO details by end of day.

Thanks,
Alison

--
Alison Reed
Head of Digital Ops, Lighthouse Retail
Alison.Reed@lighthouse-retail.com
Attachment stubs: Lighthouse_POI_Prompt_Set.xlsx (workbook), top100_skus.csv (csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-18T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC success criteria & proposed model/fallback grid

Looping in Priyom for quantization and cost modeling. My notes from Alison's questions + proposed quick plan: 

1) Cost / hallucination differences- MPT-7B-Instruct (fp16) gives us better instruction tuning and lower hallucination on task prompts vs generic Llama quant. Latency-wise MPT on a T4-class equivalent is ~1.1x faster for short contexts.
- Llama-13B-Quant (8-bit) will be cheaper per-token during peaks but tends to produce more generic completions; with strong prompt engineering and guardrails it should be fine as a fallback for factual SKU lookups (we'll validate with the SKU set).

2) Spanish regional slang- We can handle lexicon mapping via a small prompt augmentation + a lookup table in the resolver (no re-fine-tuning). For the POC, suggest adding ~150 labeled slang mappings into the prompt set and using a small hotfix mapping layer. Priyom, can you prepare a quick script to apply the lexicon and test coverage?

Action items (internal)
- Ben: validate latency on Dedicated staging (p95) using customer sample from Portland.
- Priyom: prepare quantized Llama endpoint and estimate cost delta (48-hr spike simulation).
- Marissa: prepare evaluation dashboard (accuracy, latency, escalation rate) and a quick acceptance rubric.

I'll draft a short SOW addendum after we get the attached artifacts. Target internal kickoff: Monday 2029-03-20 10:00 PT.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs referenced: POC_timeline_draft_v1.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Reed <alison.reed@lighthouse-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Markus Engel <markus.engel@lighthouse-retail.com>
Date: 2029-03-19T16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC success criteria & proposed model/fallback grid

Alison / Markus —

Thanks for the files and the clarifying questions. Quick confirmations: 

- Latency SLO: Our p95 figure includes Redwood processing + model runtime and the edge hop to our Dedicated endpoint. For customer-originated device latency (Portland office), we'll run an initial synthetic from a Portland IP and share the baseline numbers; any customer-side network variance will be documented.
- Cost delta: Priyom will run a 48-hr sim and return a per-10k-token cost estimate and expected CPU/GPU load profile for both model candidates. Expect a short write-up by tomorrow morning.
- Spanish slang: agreed — please add the 150 mappings into the same workbook (new tab) and we'll wire the hotfix mapping into the resolver for evaluation.

Next steps from Redwood (summary)
1) Internal: Ben / Priyom / Marissa to stand up trial endpoints and run baseline within 48 hrs.
2) Customer: Alison to confirm allowlist + SSO details and add slang mappings into the workbook.
3) Joint: 30-min kickoff Mon 2029-03-20 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent).

I'll circulate the draft SOW addendum today and include the acceptance rubric Ben is building. Looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
